derived.method: (1,000,000 Class A + 47,844,566 Class B beneficially owned) / (535,370,474 Class A + 59,991,242 Class B outstanding at March 31, 2026) = 48,844,566 / 595,361,716. Class B converts one-for-one into Class A, and the 10-K says holders of both classes are entitled to dividends when declared by the board; the classes differ in votes (one versus ten). Dorsey's row contains no options or RSUs (footnote 4). Computed, not stated in the filing.
